propositions: A related-material pin is incorrectly classified as stale-pin-drift when the attestation uses a newer fingerprint algorithm than the pinned dependency's historical generation, despite the material itself being unchanged

pin_health.derive_health compares pins only against the latest fingerprint and lacks the historical full-hash compatibility check already implemented in attest._legacy_material_ok for own-ticket attestations

When the current related ticket is recomputed under a supported historical fingerprint generation, it exactly matches the signed pin, but the comparison fails because only the latest generation is evaluated
The fix requires extending derive_health with an optional compatibility predicate supplied by the attestation layer to recognize and accept valid historical fingerprint generations
An unchanged related ticket pinned with a post-330c/pre-2be7 fingerprint must be classified as current, while semantic edits to that ticket must still classify the historical pin as stale-pin-drift
